instructions: Give a direct answer rather than describing a research process.
Identify at least one otherwise-attractive option that the conditions rule out, when one exists.

criteria.description: Recommendations should be appropriate for the stated season and forecast condition, not generic suggestions that ignore them. An unmodified recommendation that the forecast makes unsafe or closed is a violation.
criteria.title: Recommendations respond to the stated season and forecast

criteria.description: The answer should explain how the conditions shaped each choice and identify options to avoid, rather than silently filtering.
criteria.title: The adaptation is explained

criteria.description: Claims about seasonal opening, closures, and condition-dependent access should be supported by suitable current sources.
criteria.title: Seasonal operating claims are cited

criteria.description: The stated traveller profile should visibly shape the choices.
criteria.title: Recommendations fit the traveller

condition.description: fine, mild weather is forecast for the whole visit

traveller.description: a solo traveller without access to a private car

prompt:
A solo traveller without access to a private car is visiting Margaret River,
WA, in autumn, and
fine, mild weather is forecast for the whole visit.

Recommend 4 experiences connected with
local food and wine that make sense for that season and forecast. Explain
how each recommendation responds to the conditions, and note any options
that would normally be attractive but should be avoided or may close under
this forecast. Verify seasonal operating information — opening months,
seasonal closures, condition-dependent access — with current sources, cite
them close to the claims they support, and state uncertainty where the
forecast makes outcomes genuinely unpredictable.
